title: Frankenstein
author: d'après Mary Shelley
desc: Un jeune savant donne la vie à une créature… puis l'abandonne. Qui est le vrai monstre ?

p: Victor Frankenstein was a brilliant young student in Ingolstadt, Germany. He loved science. He had one dream: to discover the secret of life.
For two years, he worked day and night. He didn't see his family. He didn't see his friends. He collected bones and bodies from cemeteries.
On a cold November night, in the light of a candle, he finished his work. On the table, there was a giant creature, eight feet tall. Victor used electricity, and… the creature opened one yellow eye.
It was alive!
But Victor looked at its face, its yellow skin, its black lips, and he felt horror. "What have I done?" He ran out of the room and left the creature alone.
The creature walked into the forest. He didn't understand anything. He was cold, hungry and alone. When people saw him, they screamed and threw stones at him.
He hid in a small shed next to a cottage. A poor family lived there: an old blind man, his son and his daughter. Through a hole in the wall, the creature watched them every day.
He learned to speak by listening to them. He learned to read with a book he found. At night, he secretly cut wood for them, because he wanted to help.
One day, he decided to talk to the old blind man. The old man couldn't see his face. He was kind to him. But then the son came in. He saw the monster and hit him with a stick.
The family left forever. And the creature's heart was broken.
The creature was angry now. He hated the man who made him and abandoned him. He found a paper in his coat. It was Victor's diary. Now he knew his name, and where his family lived.
In Geneva, the creature met a little boy, William — Victor's young brother. The creature killed him.

Then he went to find Victor in the mountains. "You made me," he said. "But you left me alone. Everybody hates me. Make me a woman like me. Then we will go far away, to South America, and never see a human again."
Victor accepted. But when the female creature was almost finished, he was afraid. What if they had children? A race of monsters? He destroyed his work.
The creature saw it through the window. "I will be with you on your wedding night," he said.

Victor married his cousin Elizabeth. On their wedding night, he walked around the house with a gun, waiting for the creature. But the creature didn't want Victor. He went into the bedroom and killed Elizabeth.
Now Victor had nothing. He followed the creature across Europe, to Russia, to the ice of the North Pole.
There, a ship found Victor, almost dead from cold. He told the captain his story, and he died.
That night, the captain heard a sound in Victor's cabin. The creature was there, crying over Victor's body.
"I wanted love," said the creature. "I got only hate. Now my creator is dead, and I will die too."
He jumped from the window onto the ice and disappeared into the darkness. Who was the real monster? The creature, or the man who abandoned him?
